short: A destitute orphan who founded the Ming and then purged everyone who helped him.
full:
Zhu Yuanzhang was born to a tenant farming family in Anhui and lost most of his relatives to famine and disease as a teenager. He survived as a novice in a Buddhist monastery and then as a beggar before joining the Red Turban rebels against the Yuan, rising to command, eliminating his rivals on the Yangtze and proclaiming the Ming dynasty at Nanjing on 23 January 1368.

As emperor he rebuilt the countryside he had come from: land redistributed to cultivators, households registered in the lijia system, tax and population records compiled in the Yellow Registers, and hereditary military households settled on self-supporting garrison farms. He also ruled by terror. Suspecting his chancellor Hu Weiyong of treason in 1380, he abolished the office of chancellor altogether — concentrating executive power in the throne for the rest of the dynasty — and pursued the case and a second one in 1393 through purges that killed tens of thousands. He died on 24 June 1398, having outlived his heir.
